query: Help me understand what's in these airline reviews — I'm not sure which aspect is most worth analyzing.

per_column.name: sentiment_score
per_column.rationale: A continuous text-derived sentiment (VADER-style compound in [-1,1]) gives a genuine axis to group and compare reviews, directly serving an exploratory 'what's in these reviews' query. It partially overlaps with existing 'Overall Rating'/'Recommended', but sentiment computed from the review text itself is a distinct signal, not a bare positive/negative flag. Values track the text well: amazing review→0.9755, 'dreadful' seats→-0.8957, 'excellent'→0.7506, all sound readings of the source. A cluster of exact 0 values likely reflects empty/neutral rows, which is acceptable.

per_column.name: dominant_complaint
per_column.rationale: This is the strongest column for the stated goal — the analyst explicitly wants to know 'which aspect is most worth analyzing,' and a topical complaint category (staff/delay/seat/food/value/entertainment/none) is exactly the axis needed to prioritize aspects. Values are well grounded: the 'dreadful seat' review→'seat', and all positive reviews→'none'/NULL, which is the correct silent-row behaviour. The NULL vs 'none' label difference between the aggregate and per-row views is cosmetic.

per_column.name: review_length
per_column.rationale: Raw token/word count is precisely the kind of generic text-shape feature the rubric flags as adding little analytical leverage for understanding review content or choosing an aspect to analyze. It offers no new topical or evaluative axis. It is, however, faithfully derivable from the review text (counts are plausible for the sampled rows), so groundedness is high even though usefulness is low.

per_column.name: rating_sentiment_gap
per_column.rationale: Derived from the original 'Overall Rating' minus the added sentiment_score, it flags mismatches between stated rating and text tone — a legitimate, if secondary, analytical axis for an exploratory query, so not a mere restatement. It inherits dependence on both a computed column and the original rating. Values are internally consistent with a rating-derived quantity minus sentiment (e.g., 10/10-style reviews: 1.0-0.7506=0.2494, 1.0-0.9621=0.0379; bad-seat review yields a low implied rating), indicating it is grounded in table-present information.

judge.rationale: The set gives the analyst real leverage for an open-ended 'what's in these reviews / which aspect matters' question: dominant_complaint offers a topical axis to rank aspects, and sentiment_score provides a continuous text-based valence to compare against the existing star ratings, with rating_sentiment_gap surfacing rating-vs-text discrepancies. review_length is the weak link — a generic length feature with little analytical value here. Groundedness is uniformly strong across the sampled rows: sentiment and complaint labels are sound readings of the text, silent/positive rows correctly map to 'none', and the gap is consistent with the rating and sentiment it combines. No hallucinated facts observed. (Per scope rules, no penalty applied for any aspects not covered.)
